items.markdown:
`One cup of uncooked white, jasmine, or basmati rice yields about 3 cups of cooked rice`.[[1]](https://letsfoodie.com/uncooked-to-cooked-rice-calculator/)

You can find digital conversion tools like the [Uncooked to Cooked Rice Calculator](https://www.omnicalculator.com/food/uncooked-to-cooked-rice) or the [Rice to Water Ratio Calculator](https://www.omnicalculator.com/food/rice-water-ratio) to find exact portions.[[1]](https://www.omnicalculator.com/food/uncooked-to-cooked-rice)[[2]](https://www.omnicalculator.com/food/rice-water-ratio)

### Common Rice-to-Water Ratios

- **White, Jasmine, or Basmati (Stovetop):** 1 part rice to 1.5 parts water (1:1.5)[[1]](https://www.recipeone.app/rice-to-water-ratio)
- **Brown Rice (Stovetop):** 1 part rice to 1.9 parts water (1:1.9)[[1]](https://www.recipeone.app/rice-to-water-ratio)
- **Sushi Rice (Stovetop):** 1 part rice to 1.2 parts water (1:1.2)[[1]](https://www.recipeone.app/rice-to-water-ratio)
- **Rice Cooker / Instant Pot:** Use about 10% to 15% less water than stovetop methods because less moisture escapes.[[1]](https://www.recipeone.app/rice-to-water-ratio)

### Portion Guidelines

- **Per Serving:** 1/3 to 1/2 cup of dry rice per person (yields roughly 1 to 1.5 cups of cooked rice).[[1]](https://thecalculatedcook.com/rice-calculator)
- **Dry-to-Cooked Conversion:** 100g of dry rice yields about 300g of cooked rice (1:3 ratio by weight or volume).[[1]](https://www.omnicalculator.com/food/uncooked-to-cooked-rice)

If you share **what type of rice** you are cooking, **how many people** you are feeding, and your **cooking method** (stovetop, rice cooker, or Instant Pot), I can calculate the exact amounts of rice and water you need.
